subject: Region-pin risk acceptance & on-call escalation proposal
messages:
From: Evan Cheng <evan.cheng@healthsync.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@healthsync.io>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@regulus-ops.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region pin & temporary failover acceptance

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a few outstanding asks to close the SOW around region-pinning and transient cross-region processing. These are the key items they need us to sign off on before legal will execute the DPA annex: 

- Concrete operational commitment for region pin (US-only workload) and an explicit description of the conditions under which transient cross-region processing is allowed (duration, triggers).
- Subprocessors roster (full list + country of processing) and confirmation of any 3rd-party analytics/telemetry that may touch request metadata.
- KMS key control model for HealthSync data (regional keys? split keys? HSM?).
- Evidence of audit logs / access traces for transient hops for at least 90 days.

Procurement is open to a temporary, documented failover window for disaster recovery but wants a prescriptive on-call & approval flow (names/roles, SLA for rollback). Can you provide a short operational runbook and proposed risk acceptance matrix?

I attached their initial questionnaire (region-pin-questionnaire.pdf). Happy to hop on a call — Priya from Regulus (copied) will coordinate legal/procurement.

Best,
Evan
HealthSync — Head of Infrastructure

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@regulus-ops.com>, DPO Team <dpo@healthsync.io>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region pin & temporary failover acceptance

Thanks Evan — good to meet last week.

We can provide the operational artifacts you asked for. I’m attaching a first-pass runbook (region-pin-runbook-v1.pdf) and a current subprocessors roster extract. High-level responses below; detailed items are in the runbook and roster.

Summary commitments:
- Region pin: Redwood will route HealthSync production traffic to US region endpoints by default and persist your model pin on the control plane.
- Temporary cross-region processing: we can commit to a documented exception window capped at 72 hours for DR/ops migration events, with automated notification and explicit approval from HealthSync procurement (DocuSign acceptance).
- KMS: We propose customer-facing KMS segregation — regional keys by default (US key for US pin), with an option to enable split-key escrow for EU-only data if you enable EU pin.
- Auditability: all transient hops will be recorded in per-request telemetry and retained for 90 days; we will provide a log export template and an on-demand snapshot for audit reviews.

Operational runbook highlights (see attachment):
- Trigger list for transient hops (scheduled maintenance, autoscale cold-start, region outage > 60s) and a severity table.
- Approval flow: Ops engineer -> On-call lead -> Procurement sign-off for windows > 1h.
- Rollback SLA: 4 hours to revert to pinned-only routing after detection of inappropriate cross-hop.
- On-call contacts: we propose a named escalation (Rishi M., Naïomi F.) and a Regulus/HealthSync contact.

Next steps we propose:
1) HealthSync to confirm acceptance of the 72h emergency window and the approval flow.
2) We share the DPA annex draft with the KMS appendix updated.
3) We schedule a 30-min ops walkthrough with your on-call and procurement for Tuesday.

If that timeline works, I’ll circulate a DocuSign link for the exception flow and a cleaner runbook PDF.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: region-pin-runbook-v1.pdf (stub); subprocessors-roster-20261102.csv (stub)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region pin & temporary failover acceptance — technical clarifications

Kim / team — quick technical notes to close the open bullets before we send the annex: 

1) Transient hops scope: there are two classes — (A) control-plane routing decisions that briefly route a request to a compatible cache in a different region (sub-second to a few seconds), and (B) bulk failover where stream state and KV cache may be rehydrated across regions for replicas (minutes to <72h). We recommend explicitly accepting only class B under the 72h window. Class A remains within current telemetry and does not surface as cross-border processing for payload persistence.

2) KMS model: we can provide regional keys (Cloud KMS per region) and an HSM-backed split-key option for customers requiring stronger custody. Note: split-key increases operational complexity for live rollbacks; include in annex as opt-in.

3) Telemetry & audit: per-request trace id will be included in the exported audit bundle. We can produce an automated snapshot within 24 hours on request; long-tail retention for 90 days.

4) Subprocessors: the roster attached is current to 2026-11-02. Any subprocessors with access to raw request payloads are flagged in the CSV; analytics-only processors are indicated.

Operational ask for procurement: accept the 72h class-B window with the listed approval steps and commit a HealthSync signer for DocuSign. Also confirm whether HealthSync requires a shorter rollback SLA (e.g., 2 hours) — we can accommodate but need to model cost/operational impact.

I’ll join the ops walkthrough and can present the hop classification and telemetry export flow.

—Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
